stem: A 4-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department by her parents due to difficulty breathing.  The patient was in her usual state of health until this morning when she developed a fever.  Over the past 8 hours, her breathing has become more rapid and strained.  Temperature is 39.8 C (103.6 F), blood pressure is 88/64 mm Hg, pulse is 134/min, and respirations are 34/min.  On examination, the patient appears scared and has trouble swallowing.  She is sitting up on the bed, leaning forward while supported by her arms, with her head extended.  Cardiac examination reveals tachycardia and a normal rhythm without rubs or murmurs.  The abdomen is soft and nondistended.  Which of the following additional signs is most likely to be found on examination?​‌​‌​‌​​‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌​​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​​​‌​​​‌​‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌​‌​‌‌​​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​​​​​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​​​​‌‌​​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​​‌‌​​‌​​
explanation:
This child with respiratory distress is sitting in the tripod position (ie, leaning forward while supported by the arms and extending the head).  This finding indicates significant respiratory distress which, in the setting of high fever and difficulty swallowing, raises concern for upper-airway obstruction due to epiglottitis, which is a rare, potentially fatal infection classically caused by Haemophilus influenzae type b.

During inspiration, faster airflow causes a decrease in intraluminal pressure in the airways (eg, a drop in intralaryngeal pressure).  In patients with airway obstruction at the level of the larynx (eg, epiglottitis, laryngomalacia, bilateral vocal cord paralysis), this decreased pressure leads to increased airway narrowing and increased turbulent airflow, causing inspiratory stridor.

Tripod positioning helps optimize breathing by partially opening the narrowed upper airway through neck and chin extension (allows for more anterior positioning of the jaw and tongue).  It also enhances accessory inspiratory muscle function by fixing the shoulder girdle (arm bracing), thereby promoting chest expansion and reducing the work of breathing.

(Choice A)  Asymmetric breath sounds may occur with unilateral obstruction below the level of the carina (eg, foreign body aspiration) or with pleural disorders (eg, effusion, pneumothorax).  This patient's tripod positioning is more suggestive of laryngeal obstruction.

(Choice B)  Rhonchi are low-pitched rattling sounds produced when air flows through bronchi that contain excessive secretions.  Because they are caused by the movement of air through wet secretions, rhonchi can be heard during both inspiration and expiration.

(Choice C)  Expiratory stridor often occurs due to intrathoracic tracheal pathology (eg, tracheomalacia) because expiration increases intrathoracic pressure, which narrows this portion of the trachea, worsening the obstruction.

(Choices D and F)  Wheezing (ie, high-pitched, whistling noise) occurs with the constriction of the smaller airways of the lungs (eg, asthma).  Because these small airways are intrathoracic, the constriction is usually more pronounced during expiration due to the increase in intrathoracic pressure.

Educational objective:Laryngeal airway obstruction can occur with epiglottitis and leads to inspiratory stridor due to the dynamic narrowing of the larynx during inspiration; symptoms may improve when the patient sits in the tripod position, which can help maintain upper-airway patency and reduce the work of breathing.​‌​‌​‌​​‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌​​​​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​​​‌​​​‌​‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌​‌​‌‌​​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​​​​​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​​​​‌‌​​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​​‌‌​​‌​​
